“Nobody Asked. We Delivered Anyway.”

Speculative Campaign
Greggs
Self-initiated · 2025
Campaign StrategyBrand PositioningSocialOOHSpec Work
The Nation’sFirst Breakfast.
Queue.  Grab.  Go.
BrandGreggs plc
DaypartBreakfast 6–11am
Duration8 weeks
ByTanmay Dhanik

A campaign to position Greggs as the undisputed home of the working British breakfast. Not by competing with premium, but by owning the moment nobody else can claim.

Strategy

Business Problem

Greggs is already the number one brand in breakfast food-to-go but the public does not know it. Competitors like McDonald’s and Pret dominate the cultural conversation. Greggs needs to convert volume leadership into mental availability.

Campaign Objective

Drive morning footfall and breakfast consideration among 18–35 working adults in urban areas. Make Greggs the first name people think of when they think breakfast on the go.

Target Audience

Working adults 18–35. Commuters. People who eat breakfast on the move out of necessity, not aspiration. Not trying to be healthy. Trying to get through the morning.

Competitive Context

McDonald’s owns the McMuffin moment. Pret owns the commuter treat. Costa and Starbucks own coffee. Greggs owns value and warmth but has not planted its flag at breakfast yet. That is the gap.

Insight
What do we know about the audience?
“Breakfast is not a ritual for most people. It’s a problem they solve on the way to work.”
What does that mean for Greggs?
“Greggs does not need to be aspirational at breakfast. It needs to be inevitable.”
The tension we are resolving
“Everyone’s had a Greggs breakfast. Nobody’s proud of it yet. We change that.”
Creative Platform

Tone of Voice

Warm. Self-aware. Deadpan. Never aspirational. The humour comes from honesty: this is what breakfast actually looks like for most people, and that is completely fine.

Visual Direction

Real commuter environments. Early morning bus, building forecourt, pavement outside the office. Golden hour light. The Greggs bag as a recurring visual anchor. No studio shots. No smiling models.

Executions
01
OOH — Commuter Placements
Digital OOH running 5–9am only. Deadpan, time-specific copy: “6:47am. You’ve already made your best decision today.” Just the Greggs bag and the logo.
OOH
02
Social — Queue. Grab. Go. Series
Short-form video for TikTok and Reels. One person’s morning. The Greggs moment as the calm anchor. Queue shot. Grab shot. Out the door. No voiceover. Ambient city sound.
Social
03
Activation — First In Rewards
Via the Greggs app: the first 50 customers each morning unlock a discount on the breakfast meal deal. Drives early footfall, rewards loyalty, creates a reason to make Greggs the first decision of the day.
In-Store / App
04
PR — Britain’s Actual Breakfast Report
Commission a survey: what do British workers actually eat for breakfast? The data confirms what everyone knows. Greggs seeds findings to media, positioning as the honest voice on working Britain’s breakfast habits.
PR / Earned
